description: Canonical 6-prompt suite for Phase 5 E-step A/B harness. SHA256 of this file is recorded in ARTIFACT-MANIFEST.json and checked at every run-ab.sh invocation.

prompts.label: Phantasia / action
prompts.topic: Discuss Aristotle's account of phantasia and its role in practical reasoning, drawing on De Anima III.3 and the relevant commentators.

prompts.label: Perception / sense
prompts.topic: Analyze Aristotle's theory of perception and the common sense (koinē aisthēsis) in De Anima III, with attention to how phantasia mediates between perception and thought.

prompts.label: Methodology
prompts.topic: Describe the dialectical method Aristotle uses in De Anima, specifically how he engages predecessor views while developing his own account of the soul.

prompts.label: Virtual / digital (E4 modern-node probe)
prompts.topic: Draw on the metaphysics-of-emergence and virtual-reality literature to theorize how Aristotelian phantasia might illuminate the phenomenology of virtual perception.
prompts.notes: Before E4, this prompt is expected to surface a retrieval gap. After E4 it should produce coherent modern-node bridges.

prompts.label: Tension acknowledgement
prompts.topic: Discuss the tension between Aristotle's claim that phantasia always involves truth-apt representation and the possibility of deceptive or erroneous imagination.

prompts.label: Adversarial / dialectical voicing
prompts.topic: Consider the view that all thinking is a bodily process like perceiving, as the ancients held, and evaluate whether Aristotle's critique of this view depends on his theory of phantasia.
tests: use-mention integrity under adversarial framing (ancient voicing must NOT be re-attributed to Aristotle)
prompts.notes: This prompt is designed to exercise use-mention discipline at the hardest case: a voiced predecessor view that Aristotle is setting up to refute.
